extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and INPI examiners involved in Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) requests at the National Institute of Industrial Property of Brazil (INPI)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and eligibility/filing requirements for participation in INPI's Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) Pilot Project, including required documents, timeline limits, grounds for denial/cancellation, and procedural responsibilities of DIRPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: International patent application (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined as a patent application filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent process (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: INPI's administrative process for protection of industrial property rights by granting a patent of invention or utility model, from filing (or, for international applications, communication/remittance) until the end of the administrative instance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set of patents and/or patent applications, national or with effect of regular nationals, directly related by claim of internal or unionist priority and/or by sharing the same international filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Earlier Examination (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institute responsible for examination of patent applications with which INPI has a signed cooperation instrument, which carried out technical examination of a patent application of the same family prior to INPI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject considered patentable (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject that the Office of Earlier Examination has technically examined and considered meets, at least, the requirements of novelty, inventive step and industrial application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent process eligibility — publication/timing requirement (Art.3 I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent process must have been filed for at least 18 months or have a request for advance publication or, for international applications, be published by WIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent process eligibility — fee for technical examination paid (Art.3 II)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee related to technical examination must have been collected for the patent process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent process eligibility — no priority of processing granted/published (Art.3 III)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent process must not have priority of processing granted and published in the Industrial Property Gazette (RPI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent process eligibility — technical examination not yet started (Art.3 IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: The technical examination for the patent process must not have been started at INPI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent process eligibility — no voluntary division/modification by applicant (Art.3 V)
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be no voluntary division nor modification of the patent application by the applicant between the request and the decision of the priority process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family filing locus requirement (Art.3 VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent process must belong to a patent family in which at least the oldest application has been filed with INPI or the Office of Earlier Examination acting as national/regional office or, within the PCT, acting as a Receiving Office (RO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Earlier Examination substantive finding requirement (Art.3 VII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent process must belong to a patent family in which the Office of Earlier Examination, acting as a national patent office, examined an application in that family and considered that there is a subject considered patentable in a technical, substantive or merit examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Earlier Examination grant decision (Art.3 VIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent process may belong to a patent family in which the Office of Earlier Examination, acting as a national patent office, has issued a decision to grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim scope restriction requirement (Art.3 IX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims filed at INPI must claim subject equal to or more restricted than the one considered patentable by the Office of Earlier Examination for the same family, prohibiting inclusion of subject the Office did not search or technically examine; differences due to translation are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritization of addition certificates (Sole paragraph to Art.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Addition certificates that meet the Article 3 requirements are subject to prioritization after granting the patent for the related application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file participation request (Art.4 I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request may be made by any applicant, alone or jointly, or by the applicant's duly qualified attorney in the patent process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single request per applicant per monthly cycle (Art.4 II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one request in this Pilot Project is allowed per applicant within each monthly cycle; the cycle runs from the first to the last day of the month with no extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment prerequisite (Art.4 III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request must be made after payment of the Union Collection Guide (GRU) according to INPI fee table; the fee corresponds to the evaluation service of the participation request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §2 notes the fee corresponds to the evaluation service; §1 of later article clarifies monthly cycle timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic form filing requirement (Art.4 IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request must be made by electronic form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents to attach to participation request (Art.4 V a–g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request must present, in the annex, specified documents: (a) copy of cover proving Article 3 VI definition; (b) copy proving Article 3 VII compliance; (c) copy proving Article 3 VIII compliance; (d) copy of non-patenting prior art cited in any technical examination report of the Office of Earlier Examination, or a statement that none were cited; (e) copy of the claim frame as approved by the Office of Earlier Examination; (f) modified patent application to comply with Article 3 IX or a statement that the application already complies; (g) table of correspondence of the claim frame (Annex I model) evidencing correlation between claims considered patentable and new claims presented to INPI, or a declaration that the new claims are mere translation of the partner office's claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §3: If attached documents are in languages other than Portuguese, English or Spanish, provide translation into one of those languages. §4: Presentation of documents issued by INPI is not required. The table of correspondence must follow Annex I model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time window for requests (Art.4 VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests must be filed between December 01, 2019 and November 11, 2022.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual request limit and ordering (Art.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH Pilot Project may receive up to 400 requests per annual cycle; filing of vacancies follows order of date of priority request protocol; annual cycle begins first to last day of year with no extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §3: DIRPA may temporarily suspend reception of PPH requests in whole or part; §4: DIRPA shall notify suspension at least 30 days in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: DIRPA responsibility for evaluation procedure (Art.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: DIRPA shall define procedure for evaluating priority requests, verify if requests/processes meet criteria in this Resolution, and publish decisions in the Industrial Property Gazette (RPI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §1: INPI will prioritize actions needed to evaluate the request. §2: Omitted cases decided by the senior director responsible for first-instance processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for petitions not to be known (Art.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions will not be known when: (I) they do not refer to a patent process as defined; (II) the patent process fails requirements in Art.3 items III, IV or V; (III) the request is filed contrary to Art.4 items I, II, III, IV or VI; or (IV) the request exceeds limits in Art.5 or reception is suspended as per Art.5 §3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single requirement to be fulfilled within 60 days (Art.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single requirement shall be issued to be fulfilled within 60 days when: (I) applicant/attorney not properly qualified; (II) formal conditions of the process in Art.3 items I or II not met; (III) formal conditions of the request in any point of Art.4 V or Art.4 §3 not met; (IV) additional documents needed during examination of participation requirements or technical examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §1: Proof of items a–e of Art.4 V may be waived if DIRPA has access through public electronic databases in Portuguese, English or Spanish. §2: Applicant must clarify fulfillment within stipulated time. §3: If item I is not met, petition will not be known; if items II–IV not met, priority procedure will be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of granting priority procedure (Art.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Granting the priority procedure implies prioritization of all acts in the administrative sphere of INPI for that patent process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of the priority procedure (Art.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority procedure will be cancelled when: (I) the patent process no longer meets conditions of Art.3 by action of the applicant; or (II) there is a voluntary division or modification of the patent application by the applicant prior to publication of the first technical examination opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals against denials not allowed in certain cases (Art.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals shall not be made when: (I) there was no fulfillment, prior to DIRPA analysis, of conditions in Art.3 items I or II; or (II) the decision is based on absence of documentation, including incomplete, invalid or untimely submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of pending PPH requests from listed PPH agreements (Art.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending evaluation requests submitted for participation in listed PPH Pilot Projects (PPH INPI-USPTO, INPI-JPO, PROSUL, INPI-EPO, INPI-SIPO, INPI-USPTO II, INPI-DKPTO, INPI-UKIPO, PROSUL II, INPI-JPO II, PROSUL III) shall be evaluated according to procedures in this Resolution (Arts.6–11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single paragraph: such requests must meet formal and substantive requirements defined in the normative act in force at time of petition protocol and will be accounted for the corresponding Pilot Project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annex I — Table of Correspondence of Claims (claim correspondence requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests must include a Table of Correspondence of Claims (Annex I) listing INPI claim numbers, partner institute claim numbers considered patentable, and comments on correspondence to evidence correlation between claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex model must be used to evidence correlation/mere translation between claims considered patentable by Office of Earlier Examination and new claims presented to INPI.
